questions.q: What does Yahweh say about Moab?
questions.a: Terrible things will happen to the towns of Nebo and Kiriathaim, no one will boast about Moab anymore, and enemies plan to destroy Moab so that it is no longer a nation.

questions.q: Why are people crying out, wailing, and, weeping?
questions.a: They are doing these things because Moab has been destroyed.

questions.q: What are the people of Moab told to do to survive?
questions.a: They are told to run away and save their lives. They will barely survive, with nothing left, out in the wilderness.

questions.q: Why will Chemosh and his priests and leaders go away into captivity?
questions.a: The people of Moab trust in what they have accomplished and in their wealth.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen to the towns in Moab?
questions.a: A destroyer will come to every city, and no city will escape.

questions.q: What will happen to the cities of Moab?
questions.a: They will become a wasteland where no one lives.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to anyone who will not kill Moabites for him?
questions.a: Yahweh will curse him.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen to the Moabites?
questions.a: He says he will send enemies to attack them and get rid of them.

questions.q: Who will the people of Moab be ashamed of?
questions.a: They will be ashamed of their god Chemosh, just as the people of Israel were ashamed of Bethel, which they had trusted in.

questions.q: What do the people of Moab say about themselves?
questions.a: They say they are mighty, brave warriors who are ready for battle.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen to the country of Moab?
questions.a: It will very soon be destroyed.

questions.q: What should the people who live near Moab do after Moab is destroyed?
questions.a: They should mourn for Moab because Moab’s mighty rule has ended.

questions.q: What should the people in the cities of Dibon and Aroer do instead of being proud?
questions.a: The people of Dibon should come down from their place of honor and sit on the dry ground. The people of Aroer should stand beside the road and ask the people who are escaping what has happened. They should all weep and cry out because Moab is devastated.

questions.q: What punishment has come to all the cities in the land of Moab?
questions.a: Yahweh has judged every city in Moab, both far and near. He has ended the power of Moab, as if its arm were broken.

questions.q: The Moabites thought they were powerful against Yahweh, but what will Yahweh do to them?
questions.a: Yahweh will make Moab stagger like a drunk person and fall in its own vomit, and people will laugh at Moab.

questions.q: How did the people of Moab show their scorn for the people of Israel?
questions.a: They ridiculed them, treated them as though they were thieves, and shook their heads whenever they spoke about them.

questions.q: What should the people of Moab do because of their pride?
questions.a: They should leave their cities and live among the rocks, like doves that nest in the openings of caves.

questions.q: Why does Yahweh wail, cry out, and weep for the people in Moab?
questions.a: Yahweh knows that Moab’s boasting is empty, and a destroyer has fallen on Moab’s summer fruit and grapes.

questions.q: What has Yahweh done to Moab?
questions.a: He has taken away their gladness and joy and stopped the wine from flowing from the winepresses.

questions.q: Where will people cry out loudly?
questions.a: People will cry out from Heshbon to Elealeh and Jahaz, and from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath Shelishiyah. Even the waters of Nimrim will become desolate.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to the people of Moab who offer sacrifices and burn incense to their gods?
questions.a: He will put a stop to those people.

questions.q: How do the people of Kir Hareseth express their sorrow because their riches are gone?
questions.a: They shave their heads and beards, cut their hands, and wear sackcloth around their waists.

questions.q: Why is there mourning everywhere on the roofs and in the open squares?
questions.a: Because Yahweh has broken Moab like a jar that no one wants.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the attack on Moab will be like?
questions.a: It will happen quickly, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.

questions.q: How will the soldiers of Moab feel when enemies capture Kerioth and seize its fortresses?
questions.a: They will feel afraid, like a woman who is giving birth.

questions.q: How will Yahweh destroy Moab?
questions.a: Yahweh will bring terror, pits, and traps upon the people. Those who run from the terror will fall into a pit, and those who climb out will be caught in a trap.

questions.q: Why will the people flee only as far as the city of Heshbon?
questions.a: They will be too exhausted to go farther, and a fire from Heshbon will burn up the proud people of Moab.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen to the Moabites?
questions.a: The Moabites will perish and their sons and daughters will be taken captive, but in the future Yahweh will restore Moab.

commentary.text: Prophecies against Moab for pride and security. (Jer. 48:1-13) For carnal confidence and contempt of God. (Jer. 48:14-47)

Jer. 48:1-13. The Chaldeans are to destroy the Moabites. We should be thankful that we are required to seek the salvation of men's lives, and the salvation of their souls, not to shed their blood; but we shall be the more without excuse if we do this pleasant work deceitfully. The cities shall be laid in ruins, and the country shall be wasted. There will be great sorrow. There will be great hurry. If any could give wings to sinners, still they could not fly out of the reach of Divine indignation. There are many who persist in unrepented iniquity, yet long enjoy outward prosperity. They had been long corrupt and unreformed, secure and sensual in prosperity. They have no changes of their peace and prosperity, therefore their hearts and lives are unchanged, Ps. 55:19.

Jer. 48:14-47. The destruction of Moab is further prophesied, to awaken them by national repentance and reformation to prevent the trouble, or by a personal repentance and reformation to prepare for it. In reading this long roll of threatenings, and mediating on the terror, it will be of more use to us to keep in view the power of God's anger and the terror of his judgments, and to have our hearts possessed with a holy awe of God and of his wrath, than to search into all the figures and expressions here used. Yet it is not perpetual destruction. The chapter ends with a promise of their return out of captivity in the latter days. Even with Moabites God will not contend for ever, nor be always wroth. The Jews refer it to the days of the Messiah; then the captives of the Gentiles, under the yoke of sin and Satan, shall be brought back by Divine grace, which shall make them free indeed.
